modes.plain: One numeric value, such as a temperature or a loss.
modes.math: A scalar is an element x of a number system such as the real numbers.
modes.diagnostic: A zero-dimensional array has shape (); distinguish it from a length-one vector with shape (1,).

modes.plain: An ordered list of values that can represent one sample, direction, or feature set.
modes.math: A vector x in R^n has n components and supports addition and scalar multiplication.
modes.diagnostic: A vector has one axis; transpose does not turn shape (n,) into (n, 1) without reshape.

modes.plain: A rectangular grid of values, often used for a batch of samples or a learned linear transform.
modes.math: A in R^(m x n) maps an n-component input to an m-component output through matrix multiplication.
modes.diagnostic: For A @ B, the inner dimensions must agree; inspect A.shape[-1] and B.shape[-2].

modes.plain: A value container with zero or more axes; in Daedalus it may also remember how it was computed.
modes.math: A tensor here means a multidimensional numeric array with shape (d_0, ..., d_k), not the full coordinate-free mathematical definition.
modes.diagnostic: Always report value shape, gradient shape, dtype, and whether the tensor is connected to a computation graph.

modes.plain: One direction through an array, such as samples, features, rows, or columns.
modes.math: Axis i indexes dimension d_i in shape (d_0, d_1, ..., d_k).
modes.diagnostic: An axis is valid only from -ndim through ndim-1; name the semantic role of each axis before reducing it.

modes.plain: The length of every axis in an array.
modes.math: shape(X) = (d_0, ..., d_k), and the element count is the product of all d_i.
modes.diagnostic: Print both operands' shapes and label their axes before changing code; reshaping can hide a modeling error.

modes.plain: The storage format and precision used for every element in an array.
modes.math: A float32 element uses 4 bytes and has less precision and range than float64, which uses 8 bytes.
modes.diagnostic: Unexpected integer arithmetic, overflow, or precision loss often begins with an unintended dtype conversion.

modes.plain: NumPy's rule for combining compatible shapes without manually copying the smaller input.
modes.math: Compare dimensions from the right; each pair is compatible when equal or when either value is 1.
modes.diagnostic: Right-align both shapes and mark the first pair that is neither equal nor 1; backward must sum gradients over expanded axes.

modes.plain: An array object that reuses another array's memory instead of owning an independent copy.
modes.math: A view changes indexing metadata while referring to the same underlying element storage.
modes.code: view = x[:, :2]; view[0, 0] = 0  # may change x
modes.diagnostic: Use np.shares_memory and inspect .base when an in-place edit unexpectedly changes another value.

modes.plain: The collection of loss sensitivities for every element of a value or parameter.
modes.math: For scalar loss L and vector x, grad_x L = [dL/dx_1, ..., dL/dx_n].
modes.diagnostic: Check gradient shape, finiteness, norm, sign, and whether previous gradients were cleared or intentionally accumulated.

modes.plain: A table describing how every output changes with every input.
modes.math: For f: R^n -> R^m, J_ij = partial f_i / partial x_j.
modes.code: # Reverse mode computes vector-Jacobian products without materializing full J.
modes.diagnostic: If a local backward rule has the wrong orientation, compare its vector-Jacobian product against finite differences.

modes.plain: A rule for passing sensitivity backward through a sequence of operations.
modes.math: If y=f(u) and u=g(x), then dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx).
modes.diagnostic: Trace one path from loss to parameter and multiply local sensitivities in reverse execution order.

modes.plain: A record of which operations produced each value, used to compute gradients backward.
modes.math: Nodes hold values and operations; directed edges encode data dependencies for reverse accumulation.
modes.code: loss.backward()  # visits parents in reverse topological order
modes.diagnostic: A missing parent edge, detached value, or early graph release explains many absent-gradient failures.

modes.plain: Adding every gradient contribution when one value affects the loss through more than one path or batch.
modes.math: If L depends on x through paths p, dL/dx is the sum over p of each path contribution.
modes.code: x.grad = contribution if x.grad is None else x.grad + contribution
modes.diagnostic: Too-small gradients may be overwritten instead of added; too-large gradients may be stale because zero_grad was omitted.

modes.plain: Summing an output gradient back over axes where an input was repeated by broadcasting.
modes.math: Reduce leading added axes and every original axis of length 1, then reshape to the input shape.
modes.diagnostic: If bias.grad has batch shape instead of bias shape, the backward rule did not sum over expanded axes.

modes.plain: A model value changed by an optimizer during learning.
modes.math: Training searches parameter values theta that minimize objective L(theta).
modes.diagnostic: Confirm the parameter is registered once, receives a finite gradient of matching shape, and is not unintentionally frozen.

modes.plain: A group of samples processed together for one forward and backward calculation.
modes.math: A batch estimator averages or sums per-sample losses over B selected observations.
modes.code: for x_batch, y_batch in batches(x, y, size=32): ...
modes.diagnostic: Record whether the loss and gradients use sum or mean reduction because batch-size changes otherwise alter update magnitude.

modes.plain: One pass through every training sample.
modes.math: With N samples and batch size B, an epoch contains approximately ceil(N/B) optimizer steps.
modes.diagnostic: Compare runs by optimizer steps and processed examples as well as epochs when batch size differs.

modes.plain: A raw class score before conversion to probabilities.
modes.math: Softmax converts logits z into p_i = exp(z_i) / sum_j exp(z_j).
modes.diagnostic: Cross-entropy often expects logits, not already normalized probabilities; check the loss contract.

modes.plain: A function that turns class scores into nonnegative values that sum to one.
modes.math: Stable softmax uses exp(z_i - max(z)) divided by the sum of shifted exponentials.
modes.diagnostic: NaN or Inf from exp(logits) usually means the maximum was not subtracted along the class axis.

modes.plain: A number measuring how wrong the model is for the current data and objective.
modes.math: Training seeks parameters theta that minimize L(theta); reductions define how sample losses become one scalar.
modes.diagnostic: A falling training loss proves optimization progress, not generalization; also inspect validation metrics and leakage.

modes.plain: A hyperparameter controlling how far an optimizer moves on each update.
modes.math: Basic gradient descent updates theta <- theta - eta grad L, where eta is the learning rate.
modes.diagnostic: A rate that is too large can make loss oscillate or explode; too small can look flat despite correct gradients.

modes.plain: Learning details of the training set that do not transfer to new data.
modes.math: Training error continues downward while validation error stops improving or rises.
modes.diagnostic: Verify the split first, then compare train and validation curves before changing capacity or regularization.

modes.plain: Using information during training that would not be available for a genuine new prediction.
modes.math: Evaluation is biased when preprocessing statistics or labels from validation/test data influence fitted parameters.
modes.diagnostic: Trace when the split occurs and which subset each fitted transform, selection rule, or feature can observe.

modes.plain: A weighted lookup that lets each token combine information from selected tokens.
modes.math: Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k) + mask)V.
modes.diagnostic: Check score shape, scaling, softmax axis, mask convention, row sums, and whether masked weights are exactly zero.

modes.plain: A rule preventing a token from using future tokens during next-token training or generation.
modes.math: Set attention logits above the main diagonal to negative infinity before softmax.
modes.diagnostic: Inspect the upper triangle and verify future-position probabilities are zero for every batch and head.

modes.plain: A saved snapshot of model parameters and enough metadata to identify and restore them.
modes.math: A checkpoint stores an ordered mapping from parameter identifiers to arrays with exact shapes and dtypes.
modes.diagnostic: Validate format version, checksum, key order, parameter count, shape, and dtype before copying data into a model.

modes.plain: A run that produces the expected same result when its recorded environment and inputs are repeated.
modes.math: Result = f(code, data, configuration, seed, dependency versions, platform behavior).
modes.diagnostic: A seed alone is insufficient; compare code hash, data hash, configuration, Python/NumPy versions, and operation order.

modes.plain: A helper that limits ordinary learning-code mistakes with path, import, environment, output, and time controls.
modes.math: Policy constraints reduce reachable operations but do not create a kernel-level isolation boundary.
modes.diagnostic: Treat hostile or unknown code as unsafe even when the runner reports that static checks passed; use a disposable VM.

modes.plain: The files currently checked out for you to edit.
modes.math: Git compares working-tree content with the staging index and the committed snapshot.
modes.code: git status --short  # inspect worktree and index
modes.diagnostic: Separate unstaged, staged, untracked, and ignored states before deciding what a push guard should inspect.

modes.plain: The proposed contents of the next commit.
modes.math: The index is a snapshot between the working tree and the current committed tree.
modes.diagnostic: A pre-commit scan should inspect the index; a pre-push scan must inspect the exact outgoing commit range.

modes.plain: Patterns telling Git which untracked paths should normally stay out of status and staging.
modes.math: Ignore patterns filter untracked candidates; they do not remove a path already present in the index.
modes.diagnostic: If a sensitive file remains staged or committed, first verify whether it is already tracked; adding a pattern is not retroactive.

modes.plain: A recorded dependency resolution used to recreate a known environment.
modes.math: It maps direct constraints to one concrete set of direct and transitive package versions.
modes.code: # Commit the ecosystem's generated lockfile and audit changes in review.
modes.diagnostic: A manifest without a resolution may hide which transitive version is installed; compare both manifest and lockfile.

modes.plain: A public identifier for a disclosed security vulnerability.
modes.math: A CVE identifies a record; severity and exploitability are separate, contextual measurements.
modes.code: # Record CVE, affected range, installed version, fixed version, and evidence.
modes.diagnostic: Do not decide from the identifier alone; verify that the vulnerable component and code path are actually present.

modes.plain: GitHub's identifier for an advisory used by dependency and security tooling.
modes.math: An alert joins an advisory's affected version range to a dependency found in a repository graph.
modes.diagnostic: Repository alerts are server-side data and require the correct repository, enabled features, authentication, and permissions.

modes.plain: An inventory of components and versions included in a software build.
modes.math: An SBOM is a dependency graph plus identifiers and provenance metadata, not proof that every component is safe.
modes.code: # Generate SBOM from the resolved build and attach it to the matching release.
modes.diagnostic: Compare the SBOM to the built artifact and lockfile; stale inventories create false confidence.

modes.plain: Information that grants access and must not be placed in source, logs, screenshots, or public history.
modes.math: Exposure risk persists after deletion from the latest file because earlier Git objects and external copies may remain.
modes.code: token = os.environ['SERVICE_TOKEN']  # never print or commit it
modes.diagnostic: Redact the value, stop publication, rotate or revoke it, then assess history cleanup; hiding the file alone is not remediation.

modes.plain: Give a process or credential only the access needed for its current task.
modes.math: Reduce the reachable resource set and permitted operation set to lower the impact of failure or compromise.
modes.code: # Use a read-only, repository-scoped token for an alert query.
modes.diagnostic: Inspect inherited environment, filesystem roots, network access, token scope, and write permissions before execution.

modes.plain: A separate copy intended to recover data after deletion, corruption, or device loss.
modes.math: A verified backup pairs copied bytes with identity, time, source, destination, and integrity evidence.
modes.diagnostic: A successful copy log is not a restore test; restore to a new path and compare hashes before trusting the process.
